target_customer: US retail and institutional traders who want to trade on event outcomes through a CFTC regulated exchange.
problem: People could not legally trade on the outcome of everyday events in the US at scale; existing prediction markets were small, offshore or limited by no action letters.
business_model: Exchange transaction fees on event contracts, as a CFTC designated contract market.

founders.name: Tarek Mansour
founders.background_notes: Kalshi's Series A post says both founders built event driven hedging and investment products for institutional investors at Goldman Sachs and Citadel; it does not say which firm each worked at.

competitors.name: Augur
competitors.what: Decentralized prediction market on Ethereum, mainnet launched July 9, 2018 after a two year beta.
competitors.traction_then: Daily users fell sharply after launch, per Wikipedia (265 in early July 2018 to 37 on August 8).

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a matching engine and clearing for a regulated exchange, plus the legal work for CFTC designation, was heavy for a two person team; designation came in November 2020.

defensibility.rationale: CFTC designated contract market status in November 2020 made it one of 16 DCMs, a license that takes years to obtain, and liquidity on an exchange compounds.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent exchanges did not launch broad event contract markets in the sources seen; later rivals such as Polymarket and brokerages entered after 2021, and states and the CFTC contested Kalshi's contracts in 2024 to 2026 (CFTC election contract fight, circuit split between the Third and Sixth Circuits in 2026).

market_need_then: The Series A post says the company wanted event contracts to let people trade on everyday knowledge. In 2019 the only US options were PredictIt operating under a CFTC no action letter first granted in 2014, plus crypto based Augur, so a licensed exchange for event contracts was an unfilled regulatory category.

identity.logo: Wordmark with an official brand kit at kalshi.com/brandkit that bars stretching, recoloring or effects.
identity.visual_style: Clean fintech look; later celebrity and sports campaigns show only the logo, not the trading UI.
identity.voice_and_tone: Regulated and trust focused, with later social media banter against Polymarket.

branding.brand_signature: Positioned as the first CFTC regulated event exchange.
branding.community_and_virality: A 2026 CBS News story describes Kalshi using celebrity ads and World Cup campaigns to build awareness, and it sponsors Baller League USA; press also covers its social media sparring with Polymarket.

brand_strength.rationale: By 2025 and 2026 it is widely covered in mainstream press, runs celebrity and sports sponsorship campaigns and is one of two leading prediction market brands, though the strength follows regulatory wins and growth rather than the name itself.

outcome_analysis: Kalshi won the regulatory race: after YC in 2019 it got CFTC designation in November 2020, raised a $30M Series A from Sequoia in February 2021, and grew into a multi billion dollar company, reported at a $5B valuation in October 2025 and $11B in November 2025. Its edge is the exchange license plus founders with institutional trading backgrounds. The main risk is state gambling regulators, with the Third Circuit siding with Kalshi and the Sixth Circuit with states in 2026.
notes: Rounds after 2021 come from news search summaries; the Series C ($185M, $2B, June 2025, Paradigm lead) is cited to an aggregator plus a Decrypt snippet. The November 2025 round lead conflicts: Cointelegraph citing TechCrunch says Sequoia and CapitalG, other outlets say Paradigm. A $1B Series F at $22B (May 2026, Coatue) is reported by one aggregator and a Decrypt headline and is left out as unverified. No Series B was found; one directory lists an undisclosed 2022 Series B and a $787M 2022 valuation from Ingame, unverified. Seed amounts conflict across aggregators ($150K March 2019, $2M May 2019, $570K July 2019, $3.5M March 2020) and are not recorded as rounds. Founder education not found in opened sources (an aggregator mentions MIT, not verified). Kalshi.com and kalshi about pages returned 429. A search summary said the project was first called Kownig and that Kalshi means everything in Arabic, from a low quality source, left unverified. PredictIt (no action letter 2014) existed at founding but no source dated near 2019 was opened.
